```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false 
#| eval: true

# Set up chunk for all slides
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 3,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "80%"
)

options(
  digits = 2,
  width = 80,
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis",
  ggplot2.discrete.colour = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#F0E442"),
  ggplot2.discrete.fill = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#F0E442")
)

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(patchwork) 
library(kableExtra)

movies <- read_csv("movies.csv")
# preserve the historical cutoff in the brief (through December 2016)
# budgets below $10,000 and revenues of 0 are missing-data placeholders
movies_clean <- movies %>%
  filter(!is.na(release_year), release_year <= 2016,
         franchise_status %in% c("Franchise", "Original")) %>%
  mutate(franchise_status = factor(franchise_status, 
                                   levels = c("Franchise", "Original")),
         budget_clean = if_else(!is.na(budget) & budget >= 10000,
                                as.numeric(budget), NA_real_),
         revenue_clean = if_else(!is.na(revenue) & revenue > 0,
                                 as.numeric(revenue), NA_real_),
         roi_clean = revenue_clean / budget_clean,
         budget_m = budget_clean / 1e6)

# all film budgets available for parts (a) and (b)
budget_data <- movies_clean %>% filter(!is.na(budget_clean))

# only films with BOTH valid budget & revenue for financial comparison
complete_financial <- movies_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(budget_clean), !is.na(revenue_clean))

quality_summary <- movies_clean %>%
  group_by(franchise_status) %>%
  summarise(all_films = n(),
            valid_budgets = sum(!is.na(budget_clean)),
            complete_financial = sum(!is.na(budget_clean) & !is.na(revenue_clean)),
            complete_pct = 100 * complete_financial / all_films,
            .groups = "drop")
```

## Task 2 - Franchise vs. Original: Investment Strategy

### (a) Comparing the full budget distributions

Films with reported budgets below \$10,000 were treated as missing, and releases after 2016 were excluded. Both groups have right-skewed budget distributions, so the comparison uses a logarithmic scale. The plots describe all films with valid budgets, irrespective of revenue availability.

```{r}
#| label: budget-summary
#| include: false

budget_summary <- budget_data %>%
  group_by(franchise_status) %>%
  summarise(n_films = n(),
            minimum_m = min(budget_m),
            q1_m = as.numeric(quantile(budget_m, 0.25)),
            median_m = median(budget_m),
            q3_m = as.numeric(quantile(budget_m, 0.75)),
            iqr_m = IQR(budget_m),
            maximum_m = max(budget_m),
            .groups = "drop")

budget_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(minimum_m, q1_m, median_m, q3_m,
                         iqr_m, maximum_m), decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_label(franchise_status = "Status", n_films = "Valid budgets (n)",
             minimum_m = "Min", q1_m = "Q1", median_m = "Median",
             q3_m = "Q3", iqr_m = "IQR", maximum_m = "Max") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Production budgets (US$ millions)")
```

```{r}
#| label: budget-violin-plot
#| fig-cap: "Production budgets for Franchise & Original films. Both the violin and boxplot use a logarithmic budget axis."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| out-width: "75%"

budget_dist_plot <- budget_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = franchise_status, y = budget_m)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 500),
    labels = c("$0.01M", "$0.1M", "$1M", "$10M", "$100M", "$500M")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Budget (US$ millions, log-scaled)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(3, 5, 2, 5))

budget_dist_plot
```

```{r}
#| label: budget-comparison-numbers
#| include: false

franchise_budget <- budget_data %>%
  filter(franchise_status == "Franchise") %>% pull(budget_clean)
original_budget <- budget_data %>%
  filter(franchise_status == "Original") %>% pull(budget_clean)

franchise_median_m <- median(franchise_budget) / 1e6
original_median_m <- median(original_budget) / 1e6

# % of Original films whose budgets meet / exceed the Franchise median
original_above_franchise_pct <- 100 *
  mean(original_budget >= median(franchise_budget))
```

Franchise films had a median budget of \$`r sprintf("%.0f", franchise_median_m)` million, compared with \$`r sprintf("%.0f", original_median_m)` million for Original films. The distributions are right-skewed and overlapping, where **`r sprintf("%.1f", original_above_franchise_pct)`%** of Original films with valid budgets had budgets at least as large as the Franchise median. Therefore, Franchise films usually receive larger budgets, but Original productions are not exclusively low-budget films. The Franchise group is also much smaller, so the plot compares each group's distribution rather than its contribution to the overall number of films.

Franchise classification was inferred from titles and keyword tags and may incorrectly label some sequels as Original. Such errors could influence the comparison, and this would mean the true gap between Original and Franchise budgets may be slightly understated here.

### (b) 95% confidence interval for the difference in median budget

We estimated the Franchise minus Original median difference using a **non-parametric percentile bootstrap**. The two groups were independently resampled with replacement whilst retaining their original sample sizes. For 5000 resamples, the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the median differences formed a 95% confidence interval.

```{r}
#| label: median-bootstrap
#| include: false

observed_diff_m <- (median(franchise_budget) - median(original_budget)) / 1e6

set.seed(5242)
bootstrap_results <- tibble(replicate = 1:5000) %>%
  mutate(boot_diff_m = map_dbl(replicate, function(i) {
    franchise_boot <- sample(franchise_budget,
                             size = length(franchise_budget),
                             replace = TRUE)
    original_boot <- sample(original_budget,
                            size = length(original_budget),
                            replace = TRUE)
    (median(franchise_boot) - median(original_boot)) / 1e6
  }))

bootstrap_ci <- quantile(bootstrap_results$boot_diff_m,
                         probs = c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
ci_lower <- bootstrap_ci[1]
ci_upper <- bootstrap_ci[2]

tibble(`Observed median difference (US$M)` = observed_diff_m,
       `95% CI lower (US$M)` = ci_lower,
       `95% CI upper (US$M)` = ci_upper) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = everything(), decimals = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-interval-plot
#| fig-cap: "Bootstrap distribution of the Franchise minus Original difference in medians. Dashed line: observed difference. Solid lines: 95% percentile confidence limits."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| out-width: "75%"

ggplot(bootstrap_results, aes(x = boot_diff_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 35, fill = "grey", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = observed_diff_m,
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(ci_lower, ci_upper), linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrap Interval for the Median Budget Difference",
       x = "Franchise minus Original median budget (US$ millions)",
       y = "Number of bootstrap resamples") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The observed difference was **\$`r sprintf("%.1f", observed_diff_m)` million**, with a **95% bootstrap confidence interval of** $`r sprintf("%.1f", ci_lower)`-$`r sprintf("%.1f", ci_upper)` million. Since the interval lies above 0, there is evidence that Franchise films have higher median production budgets in the sampled population. The interval assumes reasonably representative and independent observations within each group, and does not account for errors in franchise classification or missing budgets.

### (c) Do the results support leadership's concerns?

To investigate budget and revenue shares fairly, the following table uses **only films with both valid budgets and revenue**. Revenue and ROI medians are calculated on that same complete-financial-record sample.

```{r}
#| label: finance-comparison

financial_summary <- complete_financial %>%
  group_by(franchise_status) %>%
  summarise(n_films = n(),
            total_budget = sum(budget_clean),
            total_revenue = sum(revenue_clean),
            median_revenue_m = median(revenue_clean) / 1e6,
            median_roi = median(roi_clean),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share_films = 100 * n_films / sum(n_films),
         share_budget = 100 * total_budget / sum(total_budget),
         share_revenue = 100 * total_revenue / sum(total_revenue))

financial_summary %>%
  transmute(Group = franchise_status, n = n_films,
            `Films (%)` = round(share_films, 1),
            `Budget (%)` = round(share_budget, 1),
            `Revenue (%)` = round(share_revenue, 1),
            `Median ROI` = round(median_roi, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(booktabs = TRUE, 
               caption = "Financial comparison by franchise status")
```

```{r}
#| label: missingness-comparison
#| include: false

quality_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = complete_pct, decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(franchise_status = "Status", all_films = "All films",
             valid_budgets = "Valid budgets",
             complete_financial = "Complete financial records",
             complete_pct = "Complete (%)")
```

The first part of leadership's concern is **partly supported**: Franchise films typically have larger budgets (median \$`r sprintf("%.0f", franchise_median_m)` million versus \$`r sprintf("%.0f", original_median_m)` million), but the significant distributional overlap means Original films should not all be treated as small projects.

The second part is **not supported as stated**. Among the `r sum(financial_summary$n_films)` films with complete financial data, Franchise films accounted for **`r sprintf("%.1f", financial_summary$share_revenue[financial_summary$franchise_status == "Franchise"])`%** of total reported box-office revenue, while Original films accounted for **`r sprintf("%.1f", financial_summary$share_revenue[financial_summary$franchise_status == "Original"])`%**. Thus Franchise films did not generate most of the sample's total revenue. Their median revenue and median revenue-to-budget ratio were nevertheless higher on a per-film basis. The higher aggregate share of Original revenue mainly reflects their much greater number of films, not demonstrated superiority of an additional Original investment.

Complete budget and revenue were available for **`r sprintf("%.1f", quality_summary$complete_pct[quality_summary$franchise_status == "Franchise"])`%** of Franchise films but only **`r sprintf("%.1f", quality_summary$complete_pct[quality_summary$franchise_status == "Original"])`%** of Original films. Reporting may be incomplete, and franchise classifications may contain errors. Moreover, the data set covers many studios, and revenue divided by production budget is not net studio profitability as it excludes marketing, distribution and cinema revenue shares. These descriptive associations should not be treated as causal effects of franchise status.

### (d) Recommendations for Meridian's next decade

1.  **Expand Original projects selectively across budget levels.** The historical Original slate includes substantial low-, medium-, and high-budget investment. Meridian can pursue creative diversity by testing more Original projects in stages, using realistic budgets and monitoring performance rather than assuming that more Original films will automatically generate more profit.

2.  **Maintain a selective Franchise portfolio.** Franchise films had higher median budgets and reported per-film box-office returns in this sample. A smaller group of carefully selected Franchise projects may complement the Original slate, but each proposal is still not a guaranteed causal franchise advantage.

3.  **Make greenlight decisions project-by-project.** Evaluate genre, production scale, expected audience, downside scenarios, and the full costs of release. Do not automatically equate Original with low-budget or Franchise with high-return. Recheck this allocation regularly, and consider errors in the franchise labels and incomplete financial reporting.
